data.title: Inside the box: Everything I did with an Arduino starter kit
data.author: lopespm
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了作者通过Elegoo Arduino Uno R3 starter kit学习电子基础概念的经历，重点探索了LED、RGB LED、74HC595扩展IC、电容平滑LED亮度变化、七段数码管和LED矩阵显示等内容。作者从最基础的点亮LED开始，逐步探索了如何使用PWM控制RGB LED颜色、通过74HC595扩展Arduino输出以控制8个LED、利用电容实现LED平滑淡出效果，以及操控单个和多个七段数码管显示数字和自定义图案。此外，作者还展示了如何在LED矩阵上实现滚动显示效果和在LCD上展示长字符串。文章通过具体代码和实践展示了Arduino在电子项目中的应用，适合初学者理解和实验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子 starter 套件的价值和使用体验

不同观点：
• **支持与积极体验**：
   - [hi_hi] 认为 starter 套件对于新手非常友好，能够降低入门门槛，激发对技术的兴趣。他通过套件学到了很多基础知识，甚至深入了解了LED和电源需求等物理原理。他还提到了模拟器和社区资源，认为这些都帮助了他更好地学习电子技术。
   - [Yenrabbit] 赞同这种入门方式，认为这些套件让新手可以在不购买大量未知部件的情况下了解各种电子能力（如传感器、马达、LED等），并期待看到更多项目成果。
   - [ja27] 补充了可编程LED（如灯带、环形灯）作为另一种有趣的实验项目。

• **对长期学习的质疑**：
   - [rs186] 认为这些玩具项目在初期会让人感到兴奋，但很快会发现它们提供的学习深度有限。他提到自己浏览了Arduino网站上的许多项目，但只有少数能激发他的兴趣。并推测很多购买Arduino和Raspberry Pi的业余爱好者最终会让设备闲置。
   - [poulpy123] 也质疑这些套件的价值，认为它们更多地教人如何使用Arduino编程，而不是真正的电子学知识。

• **关于学习路径的建议**：
   - [alabhyajindal] 作为一个完全的新手，询问这种套件是否是学习电子学的推荐途径，目标是能够通过编程点亮LED并理解背后的原理。
   - [tmaly] 提到MicroBit也是一个不错的选择，尤其是对于孩子，通过Microsoft MakeCode可以用积木式编程、Python或JavaScript进行开发。

• **对使用中国克隆版Arduino的讨论**：
   - [bityard] 指出很多便宜的Arduino套件是中国的克隆版，购买这些套件不会支持Arduino的官方开发、文档和社区等。他建议如果进一步需要开发板，可以考虑从Arduino官方渠道购买以支持其发展。

• **编程语言和开发环境的批评**：
   - [Arch-TK] 认为通过Arduino学习嵌入式开发或编程可能会养成一些不好的习惯，尤其是对没有C++经验的人来说，C++并不是一个理想的入门语言。他还提到，对于有经验的开发者来说，Arduino环境可能显得奇怪且充满不必要的hack。

• **对布线整洁的重视**：
   - [nick__m] 提到在学校学习时对布线有严格要求，认为布线的整洁与代码的格式同样重要，有助于可读性和调试。他对某些混乱的布线表示不满，认为这与编写整洁的代码类似。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户如[spapas82] 分享了自己的Arduino项目资源，提供了一个实践项目的参考链接。
• 整体上，讨论中既有对starter套件的积极评价，也有对其长期学习价值的质疑，同时涉及到了对Arduino官方支持和编程环境的批评。

44569095.article_content:
Earlier this year I saw a
Tech Ingredients episode
where a laser gimbal automatically tracks drones and shoots them down. I was fascinated by their motion control mechanism, specially the usage of a PI Controller, a high-frequency clock
Teensy microcontroller
, and their integration with custom hardware and a machine vision powered tracker.
Soon after I was researching the underlying electronics and how to experiment upon their concepts. The most obvious microcontroller to drive these would be an Arduino, but several recommendations pointed towards acquiring a kit rather than a single microcontroller, and the
Elegoo Arduino Uno R3 Starter Kit
seemed the best.
The kit contains over 200 components and an
extensive guided tutorial
, which I’ve completed (except for the last section using an extra expansion shield). In this article, I’ll go through the highlights of this journey, delightful deviations along the way, and exploration of core electronics concepts. Let’s dive in!
LEDs
Hello World: Light up a LED
I’ve been involved with electronics in different ways throughout my life, but surprisingly I hadn’t yet done its Hello World equivalent, which is to light up a LED. This simple exercise it by itself incredibly interesting that opened a series of questions:
Q: Why is a resistor needed? A: High current and increased temperature damage its delicate heterojunction structures, which eventually cause it to burnout
Q: What happens if the polarity is inverted? A: Similar to a normal diode, current will not flow and the LED will not light up. As long as this reverse power is not high, the LED will not burn and can still be used with correct polarity afterwards
Q: How to interpret its data sheet? A: There are several interesting aspects its datasheet, like the LED’s wavelength curve, operating current and voltage, etc
RGB LED [
Code
]
RGB LEDs package a red, green and blue LED inside it that can be controlled independently, allowing for wide range color representation using three
pulse width modulation (PWM)
outputs from the Arduino.
PWM is a technique used to control the average power delivered to an electrical device by varying the width of pulses in a digital signal, which when done fast enough in a visual output such as a LED, is perceived to the human eye as being of a smooth continuous amplitude, instead of a stream of single bursts.
Progressively changing the colors of a RGB LED
8 LEDs controlled via 74HC595 [
Code
]
We can attach an 74HC595 IC to extend the number of outputs possible by an Arduino, at the cost of some latency.
When writing the desired values for each of the inputs into 74HC595, they won’t be externalized until its latch is activated. Once the latch is triggered, all of the stored inputs will be externalized in one go. Very similar purpose of double buffering in video. A flicker free experience.
We are essentially controlling a piece of very limited external memory.
8 LEDs controlled via 74HC595
Smooth LED intensity fade out using capacitors
Capacitors are essentially energy stores (i.e. batteries) that with consistent charge and discharge times. By placing a condenser (or two, as in this video, so that their capacitance is summed up) in parallel with a LED, when powering the circuit both the LED immediately lights up and the condenser(s) charge in tandem. Once the main power source is removed, the condenser(s) start to smoothly discharge into the LED, creating a smooth fade out of their intensity.
Smooth LED intensity variation using Capacitors
Display
One Unit Segment Display: Digit Countdown [
Code
]
We can control this single unit seven segment display at the segment level, and in this example we sequentially write a set of segment sets that we perceive as digits.
Digit Countdown
One Unit Segment Display: Custom Patterns [
Code
]
We can also create any patterns, in whichever sequence and timing we so desire. Here are three examples of some custom patterns.
Rotation Pattern
Figure Eight Pattern
Alternating Pattern
Four Unit Segment Display: Same Character for All [
Code
]
Expanding on the above, if we write the same patterns as above on a four unit segment display, we see these replicated on all units.
Same Character for All
Four Unit Segment Display: Distinct Characters [
Code
]
In order for each of the units to present their specific segment pattern, we need to write the pattern and then select which of the units should have this pattern written to, wait for a short amount of time, and then move to the next unit, where we will do the exact same thing, only this time selecting the unit(s) that should have this pattern written.
Distinct Characters

This LED Matrix accepts an explicit bitmap, where each of the pixels is either enabled or disabled. To achieve a scrolling effect we set an offset based on value received via the potentiometer.
Scrolling through a bitmap

data.title: Xbox Hacks: The A20 (2021)
data.author: mattweinberg
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Xbox的一个硬件漏洞，即A20地址线问题，该问题源于早期Intel 8088 CPU的设计限制。最初，8088 CPU只有20条地址线，最大可寻址1MB内存。由于16位寄存器需要通过位移转换来映射到20位物理地址，当请求超出20位地址限制的内存时，地址会出现“回绕”现象，即超出部分会被截断并从低地址重新开始。

IBM在推出PC/AT时，为兼容旧系统，在主板上增加了一个A20门控信号，以模拟旧CPU的地址回绕特性。这一设计后来被沿用至包括Pentium III在内的后续CPU中。在Xbox中，利用这一漏洞可以通过控制A20地址线，使系统绕过安全启动流程，直接从闪存启动，从而带来安全风险。这一发现归功于Xbox Linux项目和研究者Michael Steil。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A20地址环绕（A20 gate）相关的历史、技术细节及其在不同系统中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• **A20地址环绕的历史和应用**：userbinator分享了一系列文章链接，探讨了依赖A20地址环绕的软件及其历史背景，指出该功能在早期的系统和软件（如WordStar等）中具有实际作用。

• **A20地址环绕的硬件实现**：messe补充了关于A20 gate如何通过键盘控制器寄存器实现切换的技术细节，认为这种设计选择可能是为了最小化硬件重新设计的工作量，是一种在嵌入式系统开发中常见的做法。

• **A20相关问题的持续存在**：mjg59提到A20相关的bug直到2009年依然存在，并分享了一个个人经历和可视化解释，展示了该问题如何在实际中出现。

• **A20在现代系统中的应用**：junon指出，构建操作系统时，仍然需要在bootloader中处理A20地址环绕问题，表明这一历史遗留问题在现代系统中仍有影响。

• **Xbox中的A20问题**：pwdisswordfishz对Xbox中启用A20功能的目的表示困惑，并指出这实际上是经过硬件修改实现的，而非Xbox原生需求。

• **推荐相关视频**：msk-lywenn推荐了一个关于解构Xbox的有趣演讲视频，暗示对了解A20及相关技术有帮助。

补充讨论：
• **对游戏平台的讨论**：heraldgeezer表达了对在Xbox上运行PS2游戏的想象，同时赞扬了Halo 2游戏的独特性，将讨论引向了游戏体验和平台对比的方向。

争议焦点：
• **Xbox中启用A20功能的必要性**：pwdisswordfishz对Xbox为何启用A20功能表示不解，并通过提供链接表明这是硬件修改的结果，而非Xbox本身设计所需。这与其他人讨论的A20在其他系统中的必要性形成对比。

总结：
讨论围绕A20地址环绕的历史、技术实现及其在不同系统中的应用展开，参与者分享了相关的技术细节、实际案例和个人见解，并延伸到了具体游戏平台的讨论。争议点集中在Xbox中A20功能的实际需求和实现方式上。

44589384.article_content:
Xbox
Xbox Hacks: The A20
4 years ago
5 min read
In November of this year (2021) we will hit 20 years since the release of the original Xbox. This console was full of vulnerabilities (or misconfiguration) from the software to the hardware and with such a low price point two decades ago for a computer - it was highly popular. For this post we are going to go into a lot of details regarding one mistake Microsoft made which was the A20.
All the discoveries and research belongs to The Xbox Linux Project and Michael Steil. Research was obtained between personal memory of the era, a
talk
and
a paper
from Steil who was known in the scene as mist.
Intel 8088 (1978) -
Credit - CPUShack
So lets start with some history with some real old CPUs starting with the Intel 8088, which thanks to the
CPUShack
reminds us it started production in 1978 and lasted till 1998. This CPU had 20 physical address lines labeled A0 through A19 and each line represents a simple binary (0/1) so you can store 2
20
bytes or 1 MB of information.
A rough drawing of address lines to RAM (A0-A19) on an Intel 8088
However, the 4 registers (code segment - CS, data segment - DS, stack segment - SS and extra segment - ES) only had 16 bits. So some form of translation needed to occur to map 16 bit registers to physical address space of 20 bits. This is where the small calculation came to be:
segment (shifted 4 bits) + offset = address
.
Internal Address -> Physical Address
So I wrote up a quick example to show how addresses translate into a physical address. Since we are shifting 4 bits, we can easily do 2
4
(2*2*2*2) and get 16 decimal or 0
x
10 hex to multiple the address by.
The thing about this notation is you can represent physical addresses with so many possible internal address + offset pairs. So knowing the early Intel 8088 only had 1MB what would happen if you asked for the memory at segment -
0
x
F800
, with offset
0
x
8000
. I'll save the long math and just say you'll get the physical address at
0
x
00100000
which is over the limit of a 20 bit address. The last real value would be at location
0
x
000FFFFF
, so the older generation CPUs just dropped any bit above the 20
th
.
So taking
0
x
00100000
would require a 21
st
bit, which doesn't exist on the Intel 8088 thus it gets dropped which ends up changing the location to
0
x
00000000
. This is known commonly as a "wraparound" because the location wraps back around to the beginning (or end) depending on how you are reading the memory.
Images from CPUShack - Intel 8028x
So the story gets interesting when you look at the history as a whole. For example, take the
Intel 80286
which still rocked a 16 bit processor, but had 16 MB instead of 1 MB memory. This meant it had 24 address lines instead of 20, which wouldn't mean much except for when IBM started building the
PC/AT
(1984). The machine had additional memory, but broke compatibility with previous solutions that depended on the implicit "wraparound" that occurred when requesting memory outside the limitation of the address lines.
If you had trouble visualizing that, the image above should show the 20 address lines on the 8088, as well as laying the additional 4 address lines that the 80286 had above. So you can see it was not possible to represent a 21 digit binary number with only 20 lines.
So IBM probably panicked at this point - they can't swap microprocessors at this point, so they tweaked the motherboard by placing a gate on the A20 address line. So depending on signal given to the gate it could be thrown to 0, thus effectively mimicking the behavior of the older Intel 8088 if warranted. This could effectively swap the system between legacy behavior or the new.
I've attempted to build an over simplified drawing to depict this, since the image above incorrectly assumes the gate exists at the CPU level, when in 1984 it did not.
Another rough drawing of the IBM PC/AT
So I think you can see where this is going now. This feature which IBM started eventually moved into the CPU and started being included in a few of the later CPUs including the Pentium series.
The lucky original Xbox was packing a 32 bit 733 MHz Intel Pentium III processor, which indeed had this A20# Gate. So knowing the Xbox boots up (after some initialization) at
0
x
FFFFFFF0
, if we ground the A20 line - the Xbox will instead boot at
0
x
FFEFFFF0
. So once again another quick and dirty drawing to explain how this will affect the process.
A partial memory map of the original Xbox
So you can see a normal Xbox boots into the secure state of the ROM. This is the portion that sets up enough critical information to verify and run the 2nd boot-loader (2BL) which then proceeds to also verify and prepare the kernel. However, grounding the A20 line proceeds to boot the Xbox directly into flash.
This is not good for Microsoft from a security perspective. The system can now boot from flash with whatever was cleverly placed there. An added bonus that booting with the A20 line grounded keeps

• **Xbox中启用A20功能的必要性**：pwdisswordfishz对Xbox为何启用A20功能表示不解，并通过提供链接表明这是硬件修改的结果，而非Xbox本身设计所需。这与其他人讨论的A20在其他系统中的必要性形成对比。

总结：
讨论围绕A20地址环绕的历史、技术实现及其在不同系统中的应用展开，参与者分享了相关的技术细节、实际案例和个人见解，并延伸到了具体游戏平台的讨论。争议点集中在Xbox中A20功能的实际需求和实现方式上。

data.author: etrez

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于编程语言Ada的历史、应用及其与其他语言（如Rust）的对比

不同观点：
• [danbruc] 指出图表的y轴未从零开始，使得差异看起来比实际大。这是一个关于数据可视化准确性的技术性评论，不直接涉及Ada语言本身。

• [tombert] 认为Ada是一种设计精良的语言，本不应该失败，并认为它应该在90年代和2000年代成为许多桌面应用程序的标准。该评论反映了对Ada语言潜力的肯定和对其实际应用未达预期的遗憾。

• [rustcleaner] 质疑Mozilla在已经有Ada/SPARK的情况下为何还要创造Rust语言，暗示Rust可能是对已有解决方案的重复发明，带有对Rust存在必要性的怀疑态度。

• [whartung] 表示失望，原本期待看到关于用Ada编写zip编码器的具体讨论，包括Ada语言在实际编程任务中的优劣。这反映了对评论内容与预期不符的不满，并希望获得更多关于Ada实际应用的详细信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Ada语言的历史失败原因及其与新兴语言如Rust的关系。部分评论者对Ada未能广泛应用感到不解和遗憾。

• 另一个值得注意的点是[whartung]对具体技术细节和案例的期待，显示出读者对实际编程实例和语言应用场景的兴趣。

• 评论中还隐含了对不同编程语言竞争和选择的讨论，特别是对新兴语言如Rust和传统语言如Ada之间选择的理由和动机。

data.title: NINA: Rebuilding the original AIM, AOL Desktop, Yahoo and ICQ platforms
data.author: ecliptik
data.article_summary: 这篇文章宣布了一个项目，旨在重现昔日的即时通讯平台，如AOL Instant Messenger (AIM)、ICQ、Yahoo Messenger和经典AOL客户端。项目团队正在努力尽可能接近原版重建这些服务，并记录整个过程。目前，AIM和ICQ已可自由使用，其中ICQ仍在开发中；AOL 4.0和5.0的支持处于alpha阶段，仅对支持者开放；Yahoo Messenger已公开可用并与Escargot网络互通。文章还提到Q-Link（Commodore 64上的AOL前身）以及提供社交平台和社区支持，包括Discord、Reddit、论坛和Wiki。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对即时通讯软件（如Jabber、ICQ、AIM等）过去和现在的技术复兴、怀旧情感及其实用性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与复兴支持者] lukaslalinsky怀念Jabber短暂兴盛的时代，认为那段时间的跨平台互通体验非常好，尽管很快结束。同时，bobsmith432提到现在有开发者在逆向工程Skype，并分享相关项目链接。
• [开源与闭源争议] fishgoesblub批评某些复兴项目未开源，并提到目前有开源的AIM服务器项目。marcodiego也质疑为何不贡献于现有的自由开源软件（FLOSS）实现，而是重新构建旧平台。
• [怀旧但怀疑实用性] iforgotpassword认为这些复兴项目虽然酷，但有点“毫无意义”，因为过去的体验无法完全重现，怀旧情绪更适合偶尔回忆。benguild同样认为，曾经的用户群体无法重现，体验无法回到过去。
• [技术与安全考虑] musicale关注现代安全威胁下的加密问题，询问在服务器系统中如何实现安全通信。
• [特定功能重要性] bastardoperator认为AOL的“个人文件柜”功能至关重要，它的消失意味着AOL的彻底消亡。
• [其他类比与现代替代] lvturner指出ICQ实际上仍在通过腾讯QQ延续。ljlolel提到Hangout.fm类似于AOL聊天室，并带有音乐功能。whalesalad则提到Adium和Pidgin作为现代的多协议聊天客户端。

补充讨论：
• [个人情感与文化影响] 多个用户（如acheron、icedchai、pjmlp）表达了对AIM等老一代即时通讯软件的怀旧情绪，部分用户认为这些软件在他们的互联网历史中占据重要位置。
• [创建新互联网] nickdothutton提出了一种更积极的观点，鼓励用户去创造他们想要的互联网，而不是仅仅怀念过去。

争议焦点：
• 项目是否值得：部分用户认为复兴旧平台是怀旧且有趣的，但实用性不强；而另一部分用户则支持这些复兴项目，认为它们有技术和历史价值。
• 开源与闭源：部分用户对某些复兴项目未开源表示不满，认为这违背了互联网自由和开放的精神。

data.title: Terence Tao: Game theory, politics and control of information
data.author: bertman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏理论的应用、复杂性及其在现实世界中的局限性和潜力

不同观点：
• [arun-mani-j] 提到他们曾尝试为游戏理论创建一个通用库，但由于游戏、策略和玩家的广泛范围，创建统一的接口非常困难，最终放弃了该计划。他们希望有人能提出更好的方法来应对这一挑战。
• [7402] 引用了Thomas Schelling的《冲突的战略》一书，指出信息不足或决策自由受限的情况下，玩家可能处于更有利的位置。这提供了一个具体的理论例子，说明游戏理论中反常现象的存在。
• [andsoitis] 提出了游戏的两种大类型：有限游戏和无限游戏。有限游戏有明确的规则和终点，而无限游戏的目的是延续游戏本身，规则和参与者都是动态变化的。
• [ls612] 作为一名经济学博士，指出游戏理论非常困难，许多研究内容受到当前知识和技术能力的限制。大多数人仅在课程中学习基础内容，深入研究的人很少。
• [like_any_other] 批评Tao低估了身份认同在游戏理论中的重要性，指出玩家会形成团队，通过操控对手的身份认同可以获得优势。
• [photonthug] 讨论了游戏理论的高层次概述和实际应用的潜力，特别是新兴的认知游戏理论和社交媒体操控模型。他们还提到现有软件工具的不足，并分享了一个有用的软件链接，强调了在AI系统中应用游戏理论的重要性。
• [noqc] 简短指出Terry呼吁不要再为错误信息问题打扰数学家，暗示某些现实问题可能超出了数学家的研究范围。
• [jablongo] 开玩笑地说Tao正在转向心理史学，暗示对未来的预测和分析可能是游戏理论发展的一个方向。

补充讨论：
• 游戏理论的复杂性和应用广度是讨论的核心，特别是如何在实际中应用和建模。
• 对身份认同和团队动态的关注，提出了游戏理论在社会和心理层面的扩展。
• 新兴领域如认知游戏理论和AI系统中的应用，展示了游戏理论在技术和科学研究中的潜力。
• 对现有工具和软件的讨论，强调了在实际研究和应用中面临的资源和方法限制。

争议焦点：
• 游戏理论在实际应用中的局限性，尤其是在处理复杂社会和心理现象时的不足。
• 关于游戏理论研究和应用的未来方向，不同评论者提出了不同的看法和期望。

data.title: Hand: open-source Robot Hand
data.author: vineethy
data.article_summary: AmazingHand项目旨在开发一种低成本（<200€）、开源、具有8个自由度的仿人机械手，适用于Reachy2机器人，但也可适应其他机器人。该手具有4根手指，每个手指由2个小Feetech SCS0009伺服电机驱动，通过平行机制控制其弯曲/伸展和外展/内收。机械手所有 actuators 都内置于手内，无需外接电缆，重量约400克，且可通过3D打印制造。控制方式有两种：使用Waveshare串行总线驱动器和Python脚本，或使用Arduino和Feetech TTL Linker。项目提供了详细的物料清单（BOM）、CAD文件、组装指南和基本演示软件。注意，实际角度可能与理论值有差异，需进一步开发智能软件以实现复杂抓取任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源机器人手的设计、应用及其技术细节

不同观点：
• 一些用户对机器人手的材料成本感到兴奋，认为当前技术进步令人振奋 ([breakpointalpha])。
• 有用户指出，手指长度不均可能是提高灵活性的关键，而非缺陷 ([arnejenssen])。
• 有人提出更倾向于非人形机器人，例如多臂厨房助理，能够根据需要增减手臂并配备各种工具 ([Brajeshwar])。
• 提到当前在机器人领域有影响力的组织和项目，如Pollen Robotics和HuggingFace ([mclau157])。
• 一位用户计划将这种机器人手改造成万圣节的装饰品，增加趣味性 ([ortusdux])。
• 强调开源硬件的进化应由社区驱动，而非封闭的生产技术 ([ChaoPrayaWave])。

补充讨论：
• 有人建议通过肌腱设计来减轻手的重量 ([amelius])。
• 有用户询问类似的外骨骼或辅助设备项目 ([agumonkey])。
• 指出世界是为人类设计的，机器人向人类方向发展能更好利用现有环境 ([binsquare])。
• 讨论了为何选择四根手指而不是五根，以及由此带来的成本和设计权衡 ([TheAceOfHearts])。
• 关注手的提升能力及其所需的改进，以提升更大重量 ([mandeepj])。
• 强调需要在手上添加敏感的传感器以实现更复杂的功能 ([glitchc])。
• 质疑人类手的设计是否是机器抓取的最佳方案，提出可能存在更优设计 ([mft_])。
• 有用户对设计的美学表示赞赏，并有意自行构建 ([SequoiaHope])。
• 有人喜欢卡通风格的三指设计，提出不同审美偏好 ([fitsumbelay])。

争议焦点：
• 机器人手是否应模仿人类手设计，还是采用其他更优设计以提升功能性。
• 四指设计与五指设计的权衡，特别是成本与功能的考量。

Amazing Hand project
Robotic hands are often very expensive and not so expressive. More dexterous often needs cables and deported actuators in forearm i.e..
Aim of this project is to be able to explore humanoid hand possibilities on a real robot (and Reachy2 is the perfect candidate for that !) with moderate cost.
=> Wrist interface is designed for Reachy2's wrist (Orbita 3D), but it can be easily adapted to other robot's wrist...
Amazing Hand is :
8 dofs humanoid hand with 4 fingers
2 phalanxes per finger articulated together
flexible shells allmost everywhere
All actuators inside the hand, without any cables
3D printable
400g weight
low-cost (<200€)
open-source
AmazingHand_Overview
Each finger is driven by parallel mechanism.
That means 2x small Feetech SCS0009 servos are used to move each finger in flexion / extension & Abduction / Adduction
2 ways of control are available :
Use a Serial bus driver (waveshare i.e.) + Python script
Use an Arduino + feetech TTL Linker
Detailed explaination are available for both ways and Basic demo software is available also.
Up to you !

Assembly Guide
Assembly guide for the Amazing Hand in combination with standards components in the BOM is here :
=> Assembly Guide
You will need simple program / script to calibrate each fingers, available here :
With Python & Waveshare serial bus driver :
here
With Arduino & TTLinker :
here
Note that this assembly guide is for a standalone Right hand.
If you need to build a standalone Left hand, you can keep the sames IDs for servos location, and select if it's a right or left hand in the software.
BUT, if you need to build both right and left hands to plug them on a robot, you will have to attribute differents IDs for right and left hands. You can't have same ID for different servos on the same serial bus...
Run basic Demo
Basic Demo which is available with both Python & Arduino.
You will need external power supply to be able to power the 8 actuators inside the hand.
If you don't have one already, simple external power supply could be a DC/DC 220V -> 5V / 2A adapter with jack connector.

Disclaimer
I noticed some variations between theorical angles for Flexion / Extension, Abduction / Adduction and angles in real life prototypes. This is probably due to several sources of variation (3D printed parts are not perfect, balljoint rods are manually adjusted one by one, esrvo horn rework, flexibility of plastic parts...).
This design has not yet bene tested for long and complex prehensive tasks. Before to be able to grasp objetcs safely (that means without damaging servos or mehanical parts), kind of smart software need to be build.
SCS0009 servos have smart capaibilities as:
Torque enable / disable
Torque feedback
Current position sensor
Heat temperature feedback
...

data.title: Doge Put Free Tax Filing Tool on Chopping Block After One Meeting with Lobbyists
data.author: josefresco
data.article_summary: 本文报道了美国国税局（IRS）的免费报税工具Direct File面临被取消的情况。该工具本应不受削减，但在所谓政府效率部门（DOGE）介入后，其命运发生变化。DOGE领导层最初对Direct File表示支持，但在与报税软件游说团体会面后，态度发生转变。DOGE成员之一、由Andreessen Horowitz支持的健康创业公司CEO Sam Corcos建议取消该工具，并与Free File Inc.（包括Intuit和TurboTax等公司）会面。尽管Direct File将在2025年报税季前保持在线，但可能明年被取消。DOGE团队包括多名与Intuit有财务关联的成员，他们参与了多个IRS项目，包括评估使用Palantir软件。这一变化引发对政府与私营企业利益冲突的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：税务申报工具及其与政府和第三方公司的关系

不同观点：
• dlcarrier认为，税务申报不应依赖类似TurboTax的独立工具，而应直接集成到IRS网站中。用户可以登录查看收入信息、补充扣除或额外收入、申诉不准确的信息，并直接申请退款或支付税款。补贴小公司与大公司竞争无法解决问题，只会加深行业壁垒和游说活动。
• Donald提到联邦承包商在DOGE方面的经验，指出资金重新分配的问题，并暗示国会听证会将揭示更多细节，可能成为公众关注的焦点。
• potato3732842指出，第三方解释税法并将责任转移给政府和纳税人，这种模式对政府有利，因此维持现状。第三方承担责任，政府避免直接与纳税人的纠纷。
• bediger4000认为，免费税务申报应成为常态，第三方营利性税务软件对公民和政府都不利。DOGE的存在并没有消除浪费，反而可能成为一个巨大的问题，最终可能被以不民主的方式处理。
• chmaynard强烈反对游说者，认为他们是只关心利益的雇佣兵，对政策没有真正的关心。
• kotaKat对IRS免费文件项目被取消感到不满，担心未来报税会更加复杂，并质疑是否需要为私人公司的高管买单。同时关心州级税务申报的延续性问题。
• chopete3建议IRS展示强制性收入列表和税务义务，以减少猜谜和误算，并认为这可以防止不正当的公司操作。
• bko认为，税务软件的复杂性和高成本源于税法的复杂性，而不是工具本身。如果政府重新编写免费税务软件，成本会转移到纳税人或IRS上。质疑政府是否能比私人公司更有效地开发税务软件，并认为简化税法是解决问题的根本途径。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应由政府直接提供免费税务申报工具，还是依赖第三方软件公司。
• 讨论中多次提到简化税法以减少税务申报复杂性的必要性。
• 对游说者和DOGE等机构的批评，反映了对政策执行和资金使用的广泛不满。
• 州级税务申报的延续性问题也被提及，表明纳税人对地方和联邦税务整合的关注。

When the
so-called Department of Government Efficiency
(DOGE) arrived at
the Internal Revenue Service
earlier this year, leaders of the group reassured workers that the agency’s free tax filing tool, Direct File, would be spared from cuts. But only a few days after meeting with tax software lobbyists, the beloved tool was placed on the chopping block, multiple sources familiar tell WIRED.
The plans to potentially kill Direct File, the free tax filing tool developed by the IRS which services 25 states, was initiated by Sam Corcos, CEO of an Andreessen Horowitz–backed health startup that has ties to SpaceX. Corcos’ suggestion to cut the popular service was presented to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in the beginning of March, multiple sources familiar say.
The weekend before Corcos suggested ending Direct File, he spoke of it positively to IRS engineers. By Friday, he had changed his tune. As sources WIRED spoke to understand it, Direct File would remain online through the 2025 tax filing season but would likely be dead by next year.
“Throughout the week, the tone had shifted,” says one source. The decision to end Direct File “came out of nowhere.”
Days after the weekend meeting, Corcos told multiple sources that he had met with Free File Inc. (previously the Free File Alliance), a group of tax preparation software companies that partner with the IRS to offer free online tax filing services. The group was organized by Intuit, which produces TurboTax, more than 20 years ago as a means of offering free filing services to lower-income taxpayers. In return, the IRS promised not to create its own government-run online filing system.
Before Inauguration Day in January and well into the following month, DOGE leadership, including Steve Davis, CEO and president of Elon Musk’s Boring Company, and Amy Gleason, acting administrator for the US DOGE Service, said they were impressed with the Direct File project and reassured the engineering team working on it that it was safe, multiple sources tell WIRED. (Though Davis stepped away from government last month, he continued to lead meetings and
deliver orders
to DOGE representatives. This included Corcos, who reportedly refused to cooperate, and Davis
attempted
to oust him.)
The IRS did not immediately respond to a request for comment from WIRED. Corcos now serves as the Treasury’s chief information officer.
“We think [the IRS] ought to wind it down, and they ought to focus their attention on other key priorities like modernization,” David Ransom, a tax lobbyist representing the American Coalition for Taxpayer Rights,
told NOTUS in April
. At least two tax preparation companies represented by the American Coalition for Taxpayer Rights, TaxSlayer and TaxHawk, also belong to the Free File Alliance. (By 2021, Intuit and H&R Block left the Free File Alliance.)
Prior to Intuit’s departure, ProPublica reported that code had been introduced into the company’s
version of the Free File website
that essentially hid the service from search engines like Google, making it nearly impossible to find without directly navigating to it.
Corcos has been one of DOGE’s primary decisionmakers at the IRS, multiple sources at the agency tell WIRED. In April, he led
a three-day workshop
with a number of representatives from Palantir to build a new “mega API” for accessing all internal IRS records. At the time, sources said the IRS was testing whether to use Palantir’s Foundry software as a central reading center for all IRS systems.
Around the time Corcos arrived as a senior adviser at the Treasury Department in late February, other DOGE members were being onboarded to the agency. Todd Newnam, who previously was a CEO of a tech company, joined as a Schedule C employee. As Corcos’ supervisor, Newnam was the DOGE team lead at the Treasury for all IRS-related matters, according to a court filing. Corcos reported to Newnam through early May, when he was named the Treasury CIO, and as stated in a separate court filing, the group worked on a variety of projects, including “reviewing of the [IRS’s] vendor contracts.” In his financial disclosure form, Newnam listed owning shares of Intuit, as
first reported
by Politico. Newnam wasn’t the only DOGE member to own Intuit shares—Linda Whitridge and Tom Krause, both at the Bureau of Fiscal Service, own shares of Intuit.

data.title: Mistral Releases Deep Research, Voice, Projects in Le Chat
data.author: pember
data.article_summary: Mistral AI推出了Le Chat的全新功能，包括深度研究模式、语音输入、项目管理和高级图像编辑等。深度研究模式帮助用户快速生成复杂话题的结构化研究报告；语音模式使用户通过说话与AI互动，无需打字；多语言推理模式提供清晰的跨语言解答；项目功能可将相关对话组织到同一空间，便于管理文件和想法；高级图像编辑功能支持对生成图像进行一致性修改。这些更新旨在提升用户体验，使Le Chat更强大、直观且有趣。用户可在chat.mistral.ai或移动应用上免费试用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具和模型（尤其是图像编辑、LLM、及其用户体验）的比较与选择

不同观点：
• **M4v3R**：认为该工具的图像编辑功能非常出色，能够在编辑时保留与查询无关的部分，避免了OpenAI模型会改变整个图像的问题。不过指出输出图像的分辨率低于输入图像，但相信未来会改进。
• **raphaelj**：尝试了多个LLM提供商后，认为Mistral的用户体验最好，没有遇到与其他提供商（如Claude或OpenAI）类似的UI错误，且功能全面、速度快，并支持禁用网络搜索。
• **trilogic**：因支持欧盟和法国的技术发展，计划在OpenAI合同结束后立即切换到Mistral。
• **tdhz77**：提出了“MRF”（Model Release Fatigue）问题，指出频繁切换大型模型带来的困扰和挑战。
• **aquir**：认为Mistral比ChatGPT或Claude便宜，并打算试用一个月。
• **behnamoh**：认为AI行业目前主要是模仿OpenAI，创新不足，各公司提供的服务大同小异。
• **monkeydust**：询问如何在多个模型上进行高风险的深度研究，是否可以通过LLM作为 judge 来评估结果，从而提升性能。
• **Aissen**：对Voxtral的发布感兴趣，但质疑是否需要LLM作为核心，还是仅需纯功能模型。
• **rawgabbit**：作为ChatGPT的重度用户，询问LeChat的使用体验和与ChatGPT的区别。
• **erlend_sh**：更关心开放且伦理来源可靠的数据模型，而非开放代码或权重，希望模型能识别所用训练数据。

44594156.article_content:
Le Chat dives deep.
Introducing Deep Research, plus Audio-in, Projects, and other updates.
Product
Jul 17, 2025
Mistral AI
AI assistants are at their best when they let you go deeper in your thinking, keep your conversation flowing, and maintain contextual continuity. Today, we’re making Le Chat even more capable, more intuitive — and more fun — with a collection of powerful new features to help you research more thoroughly, express yourself more naturally, and keep your interactions — text, voice, and images — organized in context.
What’s new in Le Chat.
Deep Research mode: Lightning fast, structured research reports on even the most complex topics.
Voice mode: Talk to Le Chat instead of typing with our new Voxtral model.
Natively multilingual reasoning: Tap into thoughtful answers, powered by our
reasoning model
— Magistral.
Projects: Organize your conversations into context-rich folders.
Advanced image editing directly in Le Chat, in partnership with Black Forest Labs.
Dive deeper with Deep Research.
Research mode turns Le Chat into a coordinated research assistant that can plan, clarify your needs, search, and synthesize. Ask a meaty question, and it will break it down, gather credible sources, and build a structured, reference-backed report that’s easy to follow.
It’s powered by our tool-augmented Deep Research agent, but designed to feel simple, transparent, and genuinely helpful, as though you’re collaborating with a well-organized research partner.
What are the top upcoming NYSE listings this year?
What are the top upcoming NYSE listings this year?
Le Chat is all ears.
Vocal mode lets you talk to Le Chat just like you’d talk to a person — no typing needed. You can brainstorm ideas while walking, get quick answers while running errands, or transcribe a meeting. It’s powered by our new voice-in model, Voxtral, and built for natural, low-latency speech recognition, that keeps up at your pace.
Thinking it through, in your language.
Think mode helps you reason through complex questions with clear, thoughtful answers, powered by our reasoning model — Magistral. Great for drafting a proposal in Spanish, clarifying a legal concept in Japanese, or just thinking things through in whatever language you’re most comfortable with. Le Chat can also code switch between languages mid-sentence.
Evaluate how the addition of augmented reality could help or hinder a furniture store, focusing on customer experience, efficiency and data.

Thought for 1s
Where Projects take shape.
Projects help you stay organized by grouping related chats into focused, context-rich spaces. Each project has its own default Library and remembers which tools and settings you’ve enabled, so things stay the way you left them. You can upload files directly into a project, pull in content from your Libraries, and keep everything — conversations, documents, and ideas — in one place. Perfect for planning a move, designing a new product feature, or keeping long-running workstreams on track.
Picture it — then edit it.
Unlike with typical text-to-image tools, you can create and then edit your images with simple prompts like “remove the object” or “place me in another city” and the model transforms the scene while preserving characters and detail. It’s ideal for making consistent edits across a series, keeping people, objects, and design elements recognizable from one image to the next.

data.title: How I Use Kagi
data.author: moebrowne
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者自2023年初以来使用Kagi搜索引擎的体验。Kagi是一个 premium 搜索引擎，不依赖广告技术，通过用户付费提供无广告、保护隐私的搜索体验。作者选择了每月14美元的Duo家庭计划，并赞赏其Lenses和Personal Results功能。Lenses允许用户自定义搜索范围，而Personal Results则可以调整特定网站在搜索结果中的优先级。作者还分享了自己创建的Lenses和屏蔽的垃圾网站列表，包括受Bobby Hiltz启发的"Flamed Fury Kagi Blog List"。通过这些工具，作者实现了理想的搜索体验。Kagi的这些功能需要登录后才能使用。

44594475.article_content:
How I Use Kagi
June 27, 2025
web
tech
What’s going on, Internet? I’ve been a happy Kagi user since early 2023 and have spent a bit of time curating my ideal Internet search experience using the tools Kagi offers.
Kagi is a premium search engine that puts you first. Unlike traditional search engines that monetise your attention through ads and data tracking, Kagi delivers clean, accurate results while maintaining complete privacy. Kagi is built on a simple principle, you're our customer, not our product.
The main selling point for me is that Kagi isn’t powered by AdTech and allows us who have the money to pay a monthly fee for a pleasant search experience. I’m paying $14 USD/month for the Duo Family plan that gives me and my wife a Professional Plan each. That alone would make me happy, nice ad free web searching. A subscription worth having.
With payment out of the way the two features I absolutely love are Lenses and Personal Results.
Lenses allow you to customise searches by specifying which websites you see in your results. Kagi provide a few Lenses by default, but you’re also able to create your own. You can create as many lenses as you want, but can only have up to 20 activated at a time at the moment.
Personalised Results allow you to block, lower, raise or pin particular websites/domains which determines how they’re showing in your search results. These are easily managed right away from the search results page by clicking on the little shield icon where each of the personalised options are available.
Kagi also make
Domain Insights
available so you can check out the most promoted or blocked domains. If you already have an account and are logged in you can easily kick start your block list from this page by toggling any of the listed domains to blocked. You can also lower, raise or pin any of the domains too.
My Kagi Block List
I’ve been curating my block list since I started with Kagi and was pretty happy with it until I came across this post
Sneaky SEO Shenanigans Suck
from Bobby Hiltz which I
bookmarked
back in January this year.
In the post Bobby describes an article he read about the decline of Google, shitty search results and how 16, yes just 16 companies dominate the web with their individual brands that plague and polute search results with crap.
This led him to
create and share a set of filters
to use in uBlacklist to use in Google and other provider searches.
I’ve taken those and added them to my existing list of domains to block within Kagi, you can find the list here,
Flamed Fury Kagi Blog List
. You can copy and paste these directly into the Kagi blocked domains in your settings page.
My Kagi Lesnes
Lenses are a fun way to search and surf the web. One of the default Lenses provided by Kagi is Small Web which allows you to search through all the websites listed on the
Kagi Small Web repo
.
I’ve made one slightly different and called it
Smaller Web
which attempts to find results in known small web communities, leprd.space, bearblog.dev, smol.pub, pika.page,
nekoweb.org
, weblog.lol,
dreamwidth.org
,
neocities.org
. This doesn’t find any homepages on these services with a custom domain, nor does it find sites like Flamed Fury who are self hosted. I feel that this can be used nicely in combination with the default Kagi Small Web lense with sites on these hosting platforms that aren’t specifically listed in the repo.
The other is
The Old Web
that lets you search through small website hosts from years gone by,
geocities.ws
,
geocities.restorativland.org
,
tripod.com
,
members.tripod.com
,
fortunecity.ws
,
angelfire.com
. I love having a search through these every now and then to see what people were saying about DMX or Limp Bizkit back in the day.
The two lense links above will only work if you’re already a Kagi member and logged in.
That’s all I have for now, catch you on the flip side!

data.title: On doing hard things
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者不擅长运动，却在去年夏天尝试划皮划艇的经历。起初，他频繁翻船，几乎一直在水里，而非船上。但随着时间推移，他逐渐感受到进步，尽管不明显——摔倒次数减少，划水声变小，船在呼吸时也不再那么晃动。他慢慢注意到水纹、风向和岸边的乌龟。从训练船到接近竞赛船，虽然仍落后于队伍，但比以前进步了。不到一年，他进入了校队，并参加了大学间的比赛，虽未获胜，但也没翻船，这让他感到意外。作者通过这段经历学会了接受在公共场合频繁出丑，并认为这种“几乎成功”的故事也有其独特的价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过坚持和微小改进实现个人目标，包括跑步、划 kayak、学习新技能等活动的经验和感悟。

不同观点：
• **bicx 的观点**：38岁开始定期锻炼，目标是保持健康而非追求高远目标。通过使用科技工具（如ChatGPT推荐的跑鞋和心率监测器）来帮助实现可量化的成功标准（如保持心率在130-160bpm之间），注重习惯的养成和持续性，而非追求短期成就。这种方法让他避免了以前的挫败感，享受到了运动的乐趣。

44560943.article_content:
On Doing Hard Things
10 Jul, 2025
I've never been known for my coordination, balance, or cardiovascular enthusiasm. In team sports, I was invariably the last one picked – probably only because "not picking" wasn't an option. Physical exertion was not among my natural strengths.
So naturally, last summer, I climbed into a boat that was both longer than my room (thanks KRH) and about as wide as myself, and tried to make it move in a straight line.
The first few sessions went about how you’d expect. I capsized enough that I began to question whether the boat was meant to be sat in at all, or if it was just a delivery mechanism for putting people into water efficiently. I spent more time in the water than I did on the boat.
But something about it stuck.
Maybe it was the scenery. The glassy water at MacRitchie at 7am looks like a mirror. There is a strange satisfaction found in failing in increasingly specific ways.
Progress in kayaking doesn’t feel like progress. You just fall in slightly less. Your stroke gets marginally quieter. The boat wobbles less when you breathe. Eventually, you start noticing things like water texture, wind direction, and the turtles on the banks. It’s less a sport than a slow, immersive calibration of self to environment.
At some point, I moved from the training boats to the “almost” racing boats. I was still behind most of the team, but less behind than before. I was nowhere near the pace of the middle school children who went there after school. My team captain encouraged me in the way good leaders do: not by pretending I was better than I was, but by acting like improvement was inevitable if I kept showing up. That assumption helped.
Less than a year in, I was told I’d made varsity. A few months after that, I competed in my first inter-tertiary race. I did not win. I did not flip. Both outcomes were equally surprising.
Kayaking taught me to be okay with repeatedly looking dumb in public.
There are worse ways to start your day than sitting on still water in a boat that doesn’t want you there, trying to move forward anyway. Turns out that’s a decent metaphor for most things.
It’s easy to over-index on success stories. But I think there’s a quiet dignity in the almost-stories too.

主要讨论点：关于亚历山大灯塔（Lighthouse of Alexandria）的历史、文化影响及相关游戏和链接资源。

不同观点：
• [evolve2k] 提到了一款开放源代码游戏《0 A.D.》，并指出灯塔是游戏中可以建造的奇迹之一。他强调了这款即时战略游戏的历史准确性，并鼓励他人尝试。
• [dochne] 提到了与灯塔有关的另一历史建筑——赫拉克勒斯塔（Tower of Hercules），该塔建于公元一世纪，并基于亚历山大灯塔的原始设计。
• [dang] 指出了文章链接的问题，说明当前链接似乎是从另一个来源复制而来，但具体来源不明确。
• [dr_dshiv] 对灯塔曾是世界上最高建筑这一事实表示惊讶，并对灯塔存续至14世纪表示惊叹。
• [echelon_musk] 提到了艺术家电脑渲染图与马赛克艺术之间的差异，暗示两者可能存在较大区别。
• [m3kw9] 提出了灯塔是否旨在吸引贸易的问题，质疑灯塔的原始功能是否与贸易相关。

• 链接问题的讨论虽然简短，但指出了信息来源的可靠性问题。

data.title: Tell HN: Notion Desktop is monitoring your audio and network
data.author: HoyaSaxa
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Notion的隐私和功能，特别是其会议检测功能及其对用户隐私的影响

不同观点：
• 支持观点1：Notion的员工[wustep]解释说，Notion仅在使用会议笔记功能时录音，并且桌面应用通过检测麦克风是否开启来提醒用户是否使用会议笔记功能。这种检测不会窃听用户对话，且相关设置可在偏好设置中关闭。
    ◦ 论据：提供了官方文档链接，并说明功能是透明的且可控的。

• 支持观点2：其他开发者[_kush]和[pat64]指出，通过检测麦克风是否使用以及网络流量来判断是否处于会议中是常见做法，并不涉及窃听实际音频流。
    ◦ 论据：类似功能在其开发的应用LookAway中也有使用，目的是为了识别会议场景。

• 中立/技术讨论：[rob74]和[like_any_other]认为，尽管这种监控可以在隐私敏感的方式下进行，但仍应提供关闭选项或改为用户主动选择加入（opt-in）。
    ◦ 论据：分析音频输入的频谱或仅监测端口而不监视实际数据是可能的。

• 反对观点1：部分用户[untech]对Notion的性能不满，但因没有找到合适的替代品而继续使用。
    ◦ 论据：性能差，但功能上仍然依赖，甚至考虑自行开发替代品。

• 反对观点2：一些用户[toddmorey]对功能设计表示不满，例如误触开启音频转录功能导致隐私泄露风险。
    ◦ 论据：实际使用中可能因设计不周导致用户隐私意外泄露。

• 反对观点3：部分用户[nihalbaig]和[chinathrow]认为这种功能设计涉及侵犯用户隐私，表示担忧甚至谴责。
    ◦ 论据：对功能缺乏透明度和用户控制表示不满，认为这种行为不道德。

• 替代方案：[Pi9h]提供了一个Notion的替代方案Docmost.com，强调无膨胀和自托管功能。
    ◦ 论据：提供实时协作、图表支持等功能，满足用户对Notion功能的需求，但允许自托管以增强隐私控制。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户[nashashmi]对Notion的功能和概念不熟悉，试图了解其基本使用和应用场景。
• 对Notion使用".so"顶级域名的质疑[scblzn]，质疑其可信度和隐私保护能力，并引用外部讨论链接支持其观点。

争议焦点：Notion的会议检测功能是否侵犯用户隐私，特别是其对麦克风使用情况的监测是否适当且透明。用户对隐私控制的自主权和功能设计的安全性存在较大关注。

data.title: When is tech not hype? Tulips, toilets, trains and tabs
data.author: alex-moon
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了科技产品中的“炒作”现象，从浏览器 tabs 到历史上的技术创新，如汽车和收音机，指出炒作并非现代独有，而是资本主义内在的一部分。作者通过 Mozilla Firefox 浏览器的例子，说明像 tabs 这样的功能在合适时机引发了广泛关注，尽管并非新技术。文章进一步分析了“炒作”在经济周期中的角色，引用了 Schumpeter 的“创造性破坏”理论和 Minsky 的“金融不稳定假说”，说明创新与投机如何推动经济周期。尽管存在炒作，但许多技术如汽车和家用电器最终仍改变了人类生活，表明炒作背后常有实质性创新。作者以厕所冲水按钮为例，强调复杂技术背后的简洁用户界面，如同工业革命的“iPhone”。

44569894.article_content:
Alex Moon
When Is Tech Not Hype? Tulips, Toilets, Trains - and Tabs
Alex Moon
15 July 2025
What do I do when I first wake up? I grab my phone. I'm reading the news, browsing Reddit, reading articles on HN, looking up the weather and anything else I might need to know about during the day. It's not until I open my tabs view, to switch back to something, that I realise I've managed to open half a dozen tabs within the space of minutes.
In 2004, Mozilla Foundation placed a two-page ad in the New York Times announcing version 1.0 of Firefox. "Are you fed up with your web browser?" the ad asks. "There
is
an alternative." Mozilla had a compelling story: in the wake of the browser wars of the 90s, in which Internet Explorer had ascended supreme over Netscape Navigator, Firefox, which started life as an experimental fork of the defeated browser, had "risen from the ashes" to defy Microsoft.
Firefox ad in the New York Times, 2004
Many users were disgruntled with Explorer at the time. Firefox boasted a number of improvements, including pop-up blocking and extensions. Perhaps the most visible difference, however, was tabbed browsing. Tabs weren't new, by any stretch of the imagination. Firefox wasn't even the first web browser with tabs. And yet, for some reason, the time was right. Browser tabs symbolised something deeper: they were a user interface for the new millennium.
What is "hype"?
Curb brokers on Wall Street, 1920s
It's so easy to talk about how tech is so scammy
nowadays
, how hype is everywhere
nowadays
as though hype were a side effect of social media or the post-truth era more generally. We would be greatly mistaken to think about hype this way. Hype is as old as capitalism. Indeed, hype is an essential component in the mechanics of capitalism broadly - arguably it is
the thing
that makes capitalism capitalism as opposed to any other currency-based economic system.
Broadly, when we talk about hype, we are talking about the so-called "business cycle". Two broad schools of thought presently dominate discourse on this macroeconomic phenomenon:
The
Schumpeterian
school, after the work of Joseph Schumpeter (1883-1950)
The
Minskyite
school, after the work of Hymen Minsky (1919-1996)
The two models were seen as contradictory for a long time. Indeed, they have largely been ignored, during the neoliberal consensus era, as "heterodox" economics. After the global financial crisis of 2009, however, renewed interest in the two theories led to increasing dialogue between them, and a period of consolidation has followed.
The
Schumpeterian
theory of the business cycle is based on the concept of "creative destruction". (It's important to say explicitly, right off the bat, that Schumpeter's "destruction" is not the same as Clayton Christensen's "disruption", which we will have cause to talk about in future posts.) Creative destruction is the process by which innovation replaces an existing technology with a new one. The most obvious example to anyone living in the 21st century is that of music media, from vinyl to 8-track to cassettes to compact discs to MP3 players to streaming.
The
Minskyite
theory of the business cycle, on the other hand, is about finance, investment and speculation. Minsky's Financial Instability Hypothesis in a few words: during times of prosperity, when debts can be paid, investors go looking for innovative instruments. Before very long, it becomes clear that some new technology is going to revolutionise the way we live. Investors start leveraging their investments, trusting blindly in the "bigger fool" who will buy for a higher price. At some point there is no bigger fool. The entire thing comes crashing down, creating a crisis. The cycle begins anew.
If like me you remember blockchain, you will recognise both of these narratives. More specifically, you will recognise both of these as narratives fundamentally about the concept of hype.
The earliest documented example of hype is the Tulip Mania of the 1630s. If we want to talk tech hype specifically, just look at the 1920s: cars, radios, and home appliances flooded into American homes. Wall Street piled into a booming economy, speculation soared, and the decade ended with the Great Depression.
But here's the thing: cars, radios, vacuum cleaners, washing machines, toasters... none of these technologies were "just hype". These were genuinely transformative innovations, and they did in fact revolutionise the way we live. Can you imagine a world without these things now? I can't.
So what's going on here?
The Infrastructure Loop
My favourite user interface has to be the flush button on a toilet. I would recommend with all my heart to anyone: have a go at fixing a toilet once in your life. You will be astounded at the complexity of the hardware involved. You will end up admitting defeat or learning more than you ever wanted to about fluid dynamics under the influence of gravity. And yet: a single button! Truly, the iPhone of the Industrial Revolution.

44569894.article_summary: 文章探讨了科技产品中的“炒作”现象，从浏览器 tabs 到历史上的技术创新，如汽车和收音机，指出炒作并非现代独有，而是资本主义内在的一部分。作者通过 Mozilla Firefox 浏览器的例子，说明像 tabs 这样的功能在合适时机引发了广泛关注，尽管并非新技术。文章进一步分析了“炒作”在经济周期中的角色，引用了 Schumpeter 的“创造性破坏”理论和 Minsky 的“金融不稳定假说”，说明创新与投机如何推动经济周期。尽管存在炒作，但许多技术如汽车和家用电器最终仍改变了人类生活，表明炒作背后常有实质性创新。作者以厕所冲水按钮为例，强调复杂技术背后的简洁用户界面，如同工业革命的“iPhone”。

data.title: Molecule produced by gut bacteria causes atherosclerosis
data.author: raphar
data.article_summary: 西班牙科学家团队15年前宣布了一项长期研究计划，旨在深入研究马德里桑坦德银行员工的心血管疾病起因。研究发现，肠道细菌产生的一种分子——咪唑丙酸（C₆H₈N₂O₂）——不仅诱发而且导致动脉粥样硬化，即脂肪和胆固醇在动脉中的积累，可能引发心脏病和中风。这一发现揭示了微生物与心血管疾病之间的因果关系，表明该疾病不仅由脂肪引起，还涉及炎症和自身免疫反应。研究人员还发现了一种可以阻断咪唑丙酸作用的药物，成功减缓了实验鼠的动脉粥样硬化进展。该研究发表在《自然》期刊上，为心血管疾病的早期诊断和治疗提供了新方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Imidazole propionate (ImP) 与动脉粥样硬化等疾病的关系，以及饮食与肠道菌群对健康的影响。

不同观点：
• **nextos**：认为当前研究的价值在于通过实验证明了ImP对动脉粥样硬化的因果关系，但媒体夸大了其新颖性。因为ImP与其他肠道菌群代谢物已被证实与糖尿病、心衰和动脉粥样硬化有关。
• **BruceEel**：指出富含蔬菜、水果、全谷物、鱼类、茶和低脂乳制品饮食的人血液中ImP水平较低，认为这是令人鼓舞的发现。
• **pretzellogician**：强调越来越多的“生活方式疾病”被归因于生物因素而非个人选择和意志力，并列举了如溃疡和动脉粥样硬化的例子，认为生活方式的影响程度值得讨论。
• **tmaly**：质疑饮食对肠道微生物的影响程度。
• **elektor**：提到西班牙科学家发起的长期研究项目，并询问美国是否有类似项目可以参与。
• **searine**：指出该研究主要由欧盟资助，美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）和桑坦德银行有少量贡献。
• **wslh**：提供原始研究的链接，供进一步阅读。
• **epicureanideal**：认为发现ImP与动脉粥样硬化的关系可能是增加健康寿命的重要进展，是迈向长寿的关键一步。
• **ck2**：提到本以为讨论的是三甲胺N-氧化物（TMAO），并提供相关研究的链接，指出营养学研究的复杂性。
• **lkuty**：质疑研究如何与食肉饮食（高脂肪、高胆固醇）相协调，并提到托马斯·考恩关于结构化水和排除区的理论，认为营养是一个复杂的问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及多个相关研究和资源链接，提供了进一步阅读和研究的线索。
• 争议的焦点包括ImP新发现的实际新颖性、饮食对肠道微生物及健康的影响程度，以及不同饮食模式（如食肉饮食）与动脉粥样硬化之间的关系。
• 研究资助来源和普通公众参与科学研究的渠道也被提及，显示出对这些方面关注。

A team of Spanish scientists made a striking announcement 15 years ago: they were seeking thousands of volunteers among the employees of Banco Santander in Madrid: researchers wanted to study them in depth for decades, in order to understand the onset of cardiovascular disease in healthy people. The results are even more surprising. Researchers have discovered that gut bacteria produce a molecule that not only induces but also causes atherosclerosis, the accumulation of fat and cholesterol in the arteries that can lead to heart attacks and strokes. This unexpected link between microbes and
cardiovascular disease
— the leading cause of death in humanity — is a paradigm shift. The work was published Wednesday
in the journal
Nature
, a showcase for the world’s best science.
The in-depth study of Santander employees using advanced medical imaging equipment soon revealed another shocking finding: atherosclerosis was ubiquitous. The volunteers were apparently healthy, aged between 40 and 55, but 63% of the participants showed signs of the disease. The new results show that some gut bacteria, in certain states, produce imidazole propionate, a simple molecule with six carbon atoms, eight hydrogen atoms, two nitrogen atoms, and two oxygen atoms (C₆H₈N₂O₂). This compound enters the blood, interacts with immature white blood cells, and triggers an inflammatory reaction in the arteries, which promotes the buildup of fatty plaques.
“Imidazole propionate induces atherosclerosis on its own. There’s a causal relationship,” asserts the biologist David Sancho, 53, leader of the new study at the National Center for Cardiovascular Research (CNIC) in Madrid. His team administered the molecule to mice, which developed the disease. Furthermore, scientists observed elevated levels of imidazole propionate in one out of every five volunteers with active atherosclerosis, the type in which fatty plaques are more likely to rupture and form the blood clots that cause heart attacks and strokes. The new results demonstrate that atherosclerosis is not only a disease caused by fat, but that it also has an inflammatory
and autoimmune component
, according to Sancho.
Aorta arteries from a healthy mouse (left), another exposed to imidazole propionate (center), and another treated with propionate and an inhibitor drug, with red staining of atherosclerotic plaque.
CNIC
The good news is that if C₆H₈N₂O₂ causes the problem in a significant percentage of patients, steps can be taken to prevent it. Researchers have identified the receptor to which the molecule binds and have managed to block it with a drug, reducing the progression of atherosclerosis in mice fed a
high-cholesterol diet
. “With this inhibitor, we completely prevented the development of the disease,” says Sancho, who has patented the experimental treatment with other co-authors, such as the Italian pharmacologist Annalaura Mastrangelo, their colleague Iñaki Robles, and the cardiologist Valentín Fuster, director general of the CNIC in Madrid and president of the Mount Sinai Fuster Heart Hospital in New York, which has borne his name for two years.
Another of the study’s authors, the Swedish biologist Fredrik Bäckhed, had already discovered in 2018 that imidazole propionate levels were higher in people
with type 2 diabetes.
And just three months ago, independent research led by the cardiologist Arash Haghikia advanced the link between the bacterial molecule and atherosclerosis. “The fact that two different groups came to the same conclusion strengthens our confidence that this is a significant and relevant discovery,” argues Haghikia, of Ruhr University Bochum (Germany). “What is particularly striking is that imidazole propionate appears to promote atherosclerosis even when cholesterol levels are normal. This could help explain why some people develop heart disease despite having few or no traditional risk factors, such as high cholesterol or high blood pressure,” he emphasizes.
Left to right: the biologist David Sancho and the pharmacologists Annalaura Mastrangelo and Iñaki Robles, at the National Center for Cardiovascular Research in Madrid.
CNIC
Cardiovascular diseases kill 18 million people each year. Banco Santander’s chairman,
Emilio Botín, died of a heart attack
four years after signing off on the project, which has allowed for the analysis of more than 4,000 volunteer workers, 400 of whom are included in this new study. The research, conducted using expensive and complex techniques such as computed axial tomography (CAT) and positron emission tomography (PET), has made it possible to detect high levels of imidazole propionate in the very early stages of atherosclerosis, which could greatly facilitate diagnosis at that invisible stage when a person is unknowingly at risk.

Chrome's SSL Bypass Cheatcode
This is Unsafe
If you type
thisisunsafe
on a Chrome SSL error page, Chrome will bypass the error and load the page for you.
Try it yourself here:
https://expired.badssl.com/
There’s no textbox to type into, just type
thisisunsafe
blindly with the page in focus.
TIP: To revert the bypass, click the “Not Secure” button in the URL bar and then click “Turn on warnings.”
History of the Bypass Code
I discovered Chrome SSL error bypass code while debugging SSL issues. I was surprised that something like that existed, and was flooded with of memories of entering
↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A
into my PS1 as a kid (see
Konami Code
).
Curiosity got the better of me, and, like Tomb Raider searching for ancient artifacts, I started digging into the history of the bypass code in Chromium.
Here’s what I found.
Danger (2014)
The bypass code was originally “
danger
,” and was added to Chromium in 2014 as part of a larger piece of work to remove duplication between
chrome/browser/resources/safe_browsing/
and
chrome/browser/resources/ssl/
.
Safe Browsing HTML/JS is in:
chrome/browser/resources/safe_browsing
And SSL HTML/JS is in:
chrome/browser/resources/ssl
But they all essentially use the same code. Merge into a single folder and remove redundancy.
Aug 11, 2014 18:03UTC - Chromium Issue #41125304
Why it was added is not clear to me, but presumably it was to allow developers to more easily bypass SSL errors during the raise of SSL-everywhere.
https://codereview.chromium.org/480393002/patch/60001/70017
/*
* This allows errors to be skippped [sic] by typing "danger" into the page.
* @param {string} e The key that was just pressed.
*/
function
handleKeypress
(
e
)
{
var
BYPASS_SEQUENCE
=
'
danger
'
;
if
(
BYPASS_SEQUENCE
.
charCodeAt
(
keyPressState
)
==
e
.
keyCode
)
{
keyPressState
++
;
if
(
keyPressState
==
BYPASS_SEQUENCE
.
length
)
{
sendCommand
(
CMD_PROCEED
);
keyPressState
=
0
;
}
}
else
{
keyPressState
=
0
;
}
}
Bad Idea (2015)
A year later, in 2015, the
BYPASS_SEQUENCE
was changed to
badidea
. There are no other changes or comments on the patch, but this change likely reflected concerns around the overuse of the bypass code; concerns that would be echoed in later years.
https://codereview.chromium.org/1416273004/patch/1/10001
.
--- a/components/security_interstitials/core/browser/resources/interstitial_v2.js
+++ b/components/security_interstitials/core/browser/resources/interstitial_v2.js
@@ -40,7 +40,7 @@
function sendCommand(cmd) {
* @param {string} e The key that was just pressed.
*/
function handleKeypress(e) {
-  var BYPASS_SEQUENCE = 'danger';
+  var BYPASS_SEQUENCE = 'badidea';
if (BYPASS_SEQUENCE.charCodeAt(keyPressState) == e.keyCode) {
keyPressState++;
if (keyPressState == BYPASS_SEQUENCE.length) {
This is not Safe (2018)
On Januay 03, 2018,
the bypass code was updated again
, this time to
thisisnotsafe
.
Unlike before, the code was changed explicitly due to growing concern around the growing popularity of being able to bypass SSL warnings in Chrome.
The security interstitial bypass keyword hasn’t changed in two years and
awareness of the bypass has been increased in blogs and social media.
Rotate the keyword to help prevent misuse.
Jan 03, 2018 03:03UTC - Chromium Issue #843085
dGhpc2lzdW5zYWZl (2018 - Present)
But then, just a few days later, on January 10, 2018,
the bypass code was changed once again
:
thisisnotesafe
was changed to
dGhpc2lzdW5zYWZl
, in what I can only guess was an attempt at obfuscation.
$
echo
dGhpc2lzdW5zYWZl |
base64
-d
thisisunsafe

+++ b/components/security_interstitials/core/browser/resources/interstitial_large.js
@@ -13,7 +13,10 @@
* @param {string} e The key that was just pressed.
*/
function handleKeypress(e) {
-  var BYPASS_SEQUENCE = 'thisisnotsafe';
+  // HTTPS errors are serious and should not be ignored. For testing purposes,
+  // other approaches are both safer and have fewer side-effects.
+  // See https://goo.gl/ZcZixP for more details.
+  var BYPASS_SEQUENCE = window.atob('dGhpc2lzdW5zYWZl');
if (BYPASS_SEQUENCE.charCodeAt(keyPressState) == e.keyCode) {
keyPressState++;
if (keyPressState == BYPASS_SEQUENCE.length) {
Along with this patch, the Chromium team released a public document titled:
Deprecating Powerful Features on Insecure Origins
.
Though it made no mention of the bypass code, it included instructions for how to bypass SSL errors during development and testing. I presume this is what was meant by the “other approaches are both safer and have fewer side-effects” comment in the code snippet above.
You can use
chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure
to run Chrome, or use the
--unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure="http://example.com"
flag (replacing
"example.com"
with the origin you actually want to test), which will treat that origin as secure for this session.

data.title: Parsing Protobuf Like Never Before
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Miguel Young de la Sota开发的高性能Go语言Protobuf解析库**hyperpb**。传统Protobuf解析器通过生成特定类型的源代码来实现高性能，但这种方法存在需预先编译类型、增加指令缓存开销等问题。Miguel通过借鉴C语言Protobuf runtime **UPB** 的动态解析特性，并针对Go语言的特性进行了深度优化，开发了**hyperpb**。该库使用了许多UPB的优化技术，如数据表驱动的解析器和内存优化，同时针对Go的独特特性（如寄存器ABI和无未定义行为）进行了进一步性能提升。测试显示，hyperpb在多个基准测试中表现优异，超越了其他Go Protobuf解析器。尽管UPB本身很强大，但由于Go与C语言交互的困难（如cgo性能问题），直接使用UPB并不理想，因此Miguel选择重写并优化了UPB的功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中FFI的性能问题、Protobuf解析优化的必要性以及相关技术选型的争议。

不同观点：
• **alexozer的观点**：指出Go的FFI速度较慢，以及针对每个Proto文件生成代码的专门化过程由于指令缓存压力导致性能不佳。他认为这些是设计VM（虚拟机）的主要动机，而不仅仅是优化代码生成或者用非Go语言实现解析器。

• **skybrian的观点**：赞同alexozer对Go内部机制导致快速解释器编写困难的分析，但认为Go团队可能并不太关注快速解释器的使用场景。如果Protobuf解析因此提速，可能会引起更多关注，从而减少对低级技巧的依赖。

• **jeffrallen的观点**：对使用高度“诅咒”的Go代码编写的新库（hyperpb）表示调侃和幽默，没有深入技术讨论。

• **mdhb的观点**：希望将Protobuf的优点引入标准化序列化格式如CBOR，并建议将gRPC-web与WHATWG streams和WebTransport结合。他认为当前的技术被奇怪的工具和假设所束缚，建议重新基于IETF和W3C标准。

• **UncleEntity的观点**：对VM设计的目的和功能提出疑问，不确定VM是针对单一Protobuf消息类型定制，还是可以解析任意Protobuf消息。他还分享了自己在二进制数据解析系统设计中的经验，认为直接采用专门VM可能是一种“过早优化”，但仍然觉得这个想法很有趣。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的技术细节包括UPB解析器、VM设计、Protobuf消息解析的优化策略等。
• 对Go语言性能瓶颈的具体分析，如FFI速度和代码生成问题，是讨论的核心技术问题。
• 关于技术选型和标准化的争议，特别是mdhb提出的基于IETF和W3C标准的建议，值得进一步探讨。
• UncleEntity提出的“过早优化”观点引发了对VM设计是否必要的思考。

Parsing Protobuf Like Never Before
Historically I have worked on many projects related to high-performance Protobuf, be that on the C++ runtime, on the Rust runtime, or on integrating
UPB
, the fastest Protobuf runtime, written by my colleague
Josh Haberman
. I
generally
don’t post directly about my current job, but my most recent toy-turned-product is something I’m very excited to write about:
hyperpb
.
Here’s how we measure up against other Go Protobuf parsers. This is a subset of my benchmarks, since the benchmark suite contains many dozens of specimens. This was recorded on an AMD Zen 4 machine.
Throughput for various configurations of
hyperpb
(colored bars) vs. competing parsers (grey bars). Each successive
hyperpb
includes all previous optimizations, corresponding to
zerocopy mode
,
arena reuse
, and
profile-guided optimization
. Bigger is better.
Traditionally, Protobuf backends would generate parsers by generating source code specialized to each type. Naively, this would give the best performance, because everything would be “right-sized” to a particular message type. Unfortunately, now that we know better, there are a bunch of drawbacks:
Every type you care about must be compiled ahead-of-time. Tricky for when you want to build something generic over schemas your users provide you.
Every type contributes to a cost on the instruction cache, meaning that if your program parses a lot of different types, it will essentially flush your instruction cache any time you enter a parser. Worse still, if a parse involves enough types, the parser itself will hit instruction decoding throughput issues.
These effects are not directly visible in normal workloads, but other side-effects are visible: for example, giant switches on field numbers can turn into chains of branch instructions, meaning that higher-numbered fields will be quite slow. Even binary-searching on field numbers isn’t exactly ideal. However, we know that every Protobuf codec ever emits fields in index order (i.e., declaration order in the
.proto
file), which is a data conditioning fact we don’t take advantage of with a switch.
UPB solves this problem. It is a small C kernel for parsing Protobuf messages, which is completely dynamic: a UPB “parser” is actually a collection of data tables that are evaluated by a
table-driven parser
. In other words, a UPB parser is actually configuration for an interpreter VM, which executes Protobuf messages as its bytecode. UPB also contains many arena optimizations to improve allocation throughput when parsing complex messages.
hyperpb
is a brand new library, written in the most cursed Go imaginable, which brings many of the optimizations of UPB to Go, and many new ones, while being tuned to Go’s own weird needs. The result leaves the competition in the dust in virtually every benchmark, while being completely runtime-dynamic. This means it’s faster than Protobuf Go’s own generated code,
and
vtprotobuf
(a popular but non-conforming
1
parser generator for Go).
This post is about some of the internals of
hyperpb
. I have also prepared a more sales-ey writeup, which you can read on
the Buf blog
.
Why Reinvent UPB?
UPB is awesome. It can slot easily into any language that has C FFI, which is basically every language ever.
Unfortunately, Go’s C FFI is really, really bad. It’s hard to overstate how bad cgo is. There isn’t a good way to cooperate with C on memory allocation (C can’t really handle Go memory without a lot of problems, due to the GC). Having C memory get cleaned up by the GC requires finalizers, which are very slow. Calling into C is very slow, because Go pessimistically assumes that C requires a large stack, and also calling into C does nasty things to the scheduler.
All of these things can be worked around, of course. For a while I considered compiling UPB to assembly, and rewriting that assembly into Go’s awful assembly syntax
2
, and then having Go assemble UPB out of that. This presents a few issues though, particularly because Go’s assembly calling convention is still in the stone age
3
(arguments are passed on the stack), and because we would still need to do a lot of work to get UPB to match the
protoreflect
API.
Go also has a few… unique qualities that make writing a Protobuf interpreter an interesting challenge with
exciting
optimization opportunities.
First, of course, is the register ABI, which on
x86_64
gives us a whopping
nine
argument and return registers, meaning that we can simply pass the entire parser state in registers all the time.
Second is that Go does not have much UB to speak of, so we can get away with a lot of very evil pointer crimes that we could not in C++ or Rust.
Third is that Protobuf Go has a robust reflection system that we can target if we des

• **mdhb的观点**：希望将Protobuf的优点引入标准化序列化格式如CBOR，并建议将gRPC-web与WHATWG streams和WebTransport结合。他认为当前的技术被奇怪的工具和假设所束缚，建议重新基于IETF和W3C标准。

• **UncleEntity的观点**：对VM设计的目的和功能提出疑问，不确定VM是针对单一Protobuf消息类型定制，还是可以解析任意Protobuf消息。他还分享了自己在二进制数据解析系统设计中的经验，认为直接采用专门VM可能是一种“过早优化”，但仍然觉得这个想法很有趣。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的技术细节包括UPB解析器、VM设计、Protobuf消息解析的优化策略等。
• 对Go语言性能瓶颈的具体分析，如FFI速度和代码生成问题，是讨论的核心技术问题。
• 关于技术选型和标准化的争议，特别是mdhb提出的基于IETF和W3C标准的建议，值得进一步探讨。
• UncleEntity提出的“过早优化”观点引发了对VM设计是否必要的思考。

data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary:
文章警告人们警惕所谓的“帕斯卡骗局”：这些信念体系或运动要求人们关注极不可能发生但可能带来巨大 positive 或 negative 后果的事件。这类骗局利用简单的预期值计算，诱导人们投入大量努力去追求极小概率的高回报事件。文章指出这类信念的三个主要问题：

1. **概率不确定性**：极不可能和极其不可能的事件难以区分，低质量证据导致概率不稳定。
2. **后果不确定性**：可能的后果多样且难以预测，容易忽视负面影响。
3. **不可证伪性**：无法通过实验验证或降低这些信念的概率。

文章建议，面对低概率高影响事件时，应避免过度依赖定量分析，而应结合定性、逻辑、法律和因果视角。最重要的是，若无法收集足够信息或提出验证方法，就不应沉迷于这种无谓的担忧或幻想。

44543630.article_content:
Beware of what I call Pascal's scams: movements or belief systems that ask you to hope for or worry about very improbable outcomes that could have very large positive or negative consequences. (The name comes of course from the infinite-reward Wager proposed by Pascal: these days the large-but-finite versions are far more pernicious).  Naive expected value reasoning implies that they are worth the effort: if the odds are 1 in 1,000 that I could win $1 billion, and I am risk and time neutral, then I should expend up to nearly $1 million dollars worth of effort to gain this boon. The problems with these beliefs tend to be at least threefold, all stemming from the general uncertainty, i.e. the poor information or lack of information, from which we abstracted the low probability estimate in the first place: because in the messy real world the low probability estimate is almost always due to low or poor evidence rather than being a lottery with well-defined odds:
(1) there is usually no feasible way to distinguish between the very improbable (say, 1 in 1,000) and the extremely improbable (e.g., one in a billion). Poor evidence leads to what
James Franklin
calls "low-weight probabilities", which lack robustness to new evidence. When the evidence is poor, and thus robustness of probabilities is lacking, then it is likely that "a small amount of further evidence would substantially change the probability. "  This new evidence is as likely to decrease the probability by a factor of X as increase it by a factor of X, and the poorer the original evidence, the greater X is.  (Indeed, given the nature of human imagination and bias, it is more likely to decrease it, for reasons described below).
(2) the uncertainties about the diversity and magnitudes of possible consequences, not just their probabilities, are also likely to be extremely high. Indeed, due to the overall poor information, it's easy to overlook negative consequences and recognize only positive ones, or vice-versa. The very acts you take to make it into utopia or avoid dystopia could easily send you to dystopia or make the dystopia worse.
(3) The "unknown unknown" nature of the most uncertainty leads to unfalsifiablity: proponents of the proposition can't propose a clear experiment that would greatly lower the probability or magnitude of consequences of their proposition: or at least, such an experiment would be far too expensive to actually be run, or cannot be conducted until after the time which the believers have already decided that the long-odds bet is rational. So not only is there poor information in a Pascal scam, but in the more pernicious beliefs there is little ability to improve the information.
The biggest problem with these schemes is that, the closer to infinitesimal probability, and thus usually to infinitesimal quality or quantity of evidence, one gets, the closer to infinity the possible extreme-consequence schemes one can dream up,  Once some enterprising memetic innovator dreams up a Pascal's scam, the probabilities or consequences of these possible futures can be greatly exaggerated yet still seem plausible. "Yes, but
what if
?" the carrier of such a mind-virus incessantly demands.  Furthermore, since more than a few disasters are indeed low probability events (e.g. 9/11), the plausibility and importance of dealing with such risks seems to grow in importance after they occur -- the occurrence of one improbable disaster leads to paranoia about a large number of others, and similarly for fortuitous windfalls and hopes. Humanity can dream up a near-infinity of Pascal's scams, or spend a near-infinity of time fruitlessly worrying about them or hoping for them. There are however far better ways to spend one's time -- for example in thinking about what has actually happened in the real world, rather than the vast number of things that might happen in the future but quite probably won't, or will likely cause consequences very differently than you expect.
So how should we approach low probability hypotheses with potential high value (negative or positive) outcomes?  Franklin et. al.
suggest
that "[t]he strongly quantitative style of education in statistics, valuable as it is, can lead to a neglect of the more qualitative, logical, legal and causal perspectives needed to understand data intelligently. That is especially so in extreme risk analysis, where there is a lack of large data sets to ground solidly quantitative conclusions, and correspondingly a need to supplement the data with outside information and with argument on individual data points."
On the above quoted points I agree with Franklin, and add a more blunt suggestion: stop throwing around long odds and dreaming of big consequences as if you are onto something profound.  If you can't gather the information needed to reduce the uncertainties, and if you can't suggest experiments to make the hope or worry falsifiable, stop nightmaring or daydreaming already. data.title: Trump's war against NPR and PBS notches win as Senate votes to kill funding
data.author: duxup
data.article_summary: 美国参议院以51-48票通过决议，取消了对公共广播公司（CPB）两年共计11亿美元的 funding，影响公共广播和电视站。该资金用于支持全国公共广播电台（NPR）和公共电视网（PBS），其中包括升级广播系统和基础设施。取消联邦 funding 将导致许多地方公共广播和电视站面临关闭，影响高质量教育节目和紧急警报服务。参议院还通过了其他机构的削减，总额达94亿美元。民主党试图保留公共广播 funding 的修正案被否决。白宫此前要求结束对NPR和PBS的资助，称其传播偏见信息。众议院将对此进行最终表决，公共电视站呼吁阻止削减 funding，否则2025年10月1日起资金将彻底切断。

主要讨论点：公共广播电视机构（PBS）和国家公共广播电台（NPR）的政府资助及其作用

不同观点：
• [legitster的观点]  
   1. 政府资助并没有直接用于PBS的节目制作，而是用于维持地方电视台的运营，特别是在农村地区。  
   2. 这些地方电视台利用资助来维持运营，并可以购买NPR或PBS的内容。  
   3. PBS和NPR自己制作的内容通常是最不具争议性和最客观的报道。  
   4. 争议在于地方电视台自己播放的内容往往更具倾向性，但农村地区的政客往往希望完全取消这些声音。

• [ta8645的观点]  
   1. PBS和NPR即使没有政府资助也能很好地生存。  
   2. 它们深受观众喜爱，可以通过私人资助获得支持。

The US Senate voted to rescind two years' worth of funding from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB), delivering a blow to public radio and television stations around the country. The CPB is a publicly funded nonprofit corporation that supports NPR and PBS stations.
The
51-48 vote
today on President Trump's rescissions package would eliminate $1.1 billion that was allocated to public broadcasting for fiscal years 2026 and 2027. All 51 yes votes came from Republicans, while Sens. Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) voted against. The $1.1 billion
includes
$60 million for "costs associated with replacing and upgrading the public broadcasting interconnection system" and other back-end infrastructure for public media.
"Without federal funding, many local public radio and television stations will be forced to shut down. Parents will have fewer high quality learning resources available for their children," CPB CEO Patricia Harrison
said
. "Millions of Americans will have less trustworthy information about their communities, states, country, and world with which to make decisions about the quality of their lives. Cutting federal funding could also put Americans at risk of losing national and local emergency alerts that serve as a lifeline to many Americans in times of severe need."
The
Rescissions Act
also targets the State Department, the US Agency for International Development (USAID), and other agencies, rescinding $9.4 billion overall. "The senate's approval of the cuts tees up a final showdown in the House, which approved an earlier version last month,"
NPR wrote
.
An
amendment
by Sen. Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.) to preserve public broadcasting funding was rejected in a 52-47 vote. Murkowski, who expressed concern about emergency alerts during disasters, was the only Republican to vote for that amendment. Murkowski separately proposed an amendment "to restore CPB funding while barring any federal money from going to NPR," but it was defeated, NPR wrote.
“Republicans bent knee to wannabe King Donald”
Democrats slammed Republicans before and after the votes. "In the middle of the night, Republicans once again bent the knee to their wannabe King Donald, rubber-stamping his cruel and callous cuts while robbing kids and communities of free, high quality public programming," Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.)
said
. "By eliminating public media funding, Republicans are silencing rural broadcasters. They are stripping communities of essential emergency alert infrastructure. They are taking away trusted educational programming from millions of children."
The White House called for an end to federal funding for NPR and PBS in April,
claiming
that they "spread radical, woke propaganda disguised as 'news.'" Trump also fired the CPB's three Democratic board members, who refused to leave their posts. Trump
sued them this week
in an attempt to force them out.
Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) said during debate that public broadcasting "has long been overtaken by partisan activists," according to NPR. Cruz said that "NPR and PBS have revealed their left-wing bias time and time again. If you want to watch the left-wing propaganda, turn on MSNBC. But the taxpayers should not be forced to subsidize it."
America's Public Television Stations, a membership group representing public stations,
said
it is "devastated that the Senate voted to eliminate federal funding to the local public television stations throughout this country... This elimination of federal funding will decimate public media and put local stations at risk of going dark, cutting off service to communities that rely on them—many of which have no other access to locally controlled media."
The group urged the House to stop the cuts before they take effect in a few months. "As the rescissions package moves back to the House for its final consideration, we urge the House to oppose the package and the elimination of public media," the group said. "If this package passes the House, all funding to local stations will be cut off starting October 1, 2025 and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting will shut down."
CPB expenses
in fiscal year 2025 are $545 million, of which 66.9 percent goes to TV programming. Another 22.3 percent goes to radio programming, while the rest is for administration and support.
The CPB
distributes over 70 percent
of its funding to about 1,500 public radio and TV stations. Those stations pay fees to NPR and PBS, which also get money from sponsorships, donations, and grants.
Emergency alerts system at risk
Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) talked about the funding's impact on emergency alerts in a
speech
from the Senate floor. Stations "running on backup generators are built to broadcast through disasters" and can send alerts even when people don't have Internet access, she said. Cantwell said that

• PBS WARN系统在紧急警报传输中的作用，以及其在2024年发送的超过11,000条无线紧急警报（WEAs）的数据，显示了其在公共安全中的重要性。  
• 关于地方电视台内容的倾向性问题，特别是地方政客对内容的影响和干预意图。  
• 政府资助的使用细节及其对农村地区公共广播服务的影响。

data.title: Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models Tech Report 2025
data.author: 2bit
data.article_summary: 苹果公司在2025年发布的技术报告中介绍了其最新的多语言、多模态基础语言模型，包括一个约30亿参数的设备端模型和一个基于平行轨道混合专家（PT-MoE）架构的服务器端模型。设备端模型通过KV-cache共享和2-bit量化训练优化，适用于Apple Silicon芯片；服务器端模型则结合了轨道并行、专家混合稀疏计算及全局-局部交错注意力机制，运行于Apple私有云计算平台。这些模型通过大规模多语言、多模态数据集进行训练，并采用监督微调和强化学习进一步优化。新模型支持更多语言，并能理解图像和执行工具调用。在公共基准测试和人工评估中，这些模型的表现优于或相当于同类开放基准。开发者可通过Swift语言的Foundation Models框架轻松集成这些功能，且模型遵循负责任的AI原则，保障用户隐私并进行内容过滤。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple在AI模型和Siri上的进展、技术研发与实际应用之间的差距、隐私与数据安全问题、与竞争对手的比较

不同观点：
• Perfmode强调Apple在训练模型时使用多样化且高质量的数据，并且不使用用户的私人数据，同时采取措施过滤敏感信息，遵循道德爬取规则。这表明Apple在数据隐私和伦理方面的努力。
• Mittermayr抱怨Siri在处理基本任务时表现不佳，尽管Apple在研究和讨论AI技术，但在实际应用中（如温度转换）仍未见显著改进，这引发对Apple千元设备实用性的质疑。
• Devinprater指出Apple在无障碍功能方面的落后，例如Google已在屏幕阅读器中实现AI图像描述，而Apple作为“无障碍之王”在这方面表现不足。
• ApolloVonZ支持Apple在Swift语言中集成AI模型的做法，认为这简化了开发者的工作，并强调Apple在结构化数据处理方面的优势，尽管进展缓慢但仍有潜力。
• Jonplackett质疑Apple为何在Siri尚未使用新模型的情况下将技术提供给开发者，暗示对技术成熟度的担忧。
• Yalogin认为Apple发布研究成果是为了展示其在AI方面的能力，但尚未在实际产品中整合这些技术，缺乏对用户的实际价值。
• Chevman通过个人经历（与11岁儿子测试Siri失败）强调Siri的不足，呼吁Apple尽快改进。
• LeicaLatte对Apple产品整合的失败表示失望，怀念乔布斯时代的“产品即用”哲学，而非现在的“复杂文档解释”。
• Frankfrank13怀疑Apple是否出于法律或营销原因强调其模型数据来源的合规性。
• Mensetmanusman认为Apple因数据中心不足和设备数量庞大而难以运行复杂模型，且在设备上运行模型存在性能风险。
• Jiehong希望Apple改进语音识别和多语言转录功能，强调实际使用体验的提升。
• JacobJack期待在消费级硬件上运行Apple的模型，表达对小型模型能力的信心。
• Bitpush认为Apple在AI领域落后于其他公司（如OpenAI、Google），对其曾经的宏大宣示和当前表现之间的差距感到失望。
• JKCalhoun期待未来iPhone硬件能支持这些模型，提出“aiPhone”的概念。
• Sneilan1对Apple展示小型模型能力的前景感到兴奋，希望其能证明小型模型与大型模型一样 capable。

补充讨论：
• Apple在AI模型研究与实际应用之间的差距是多个评论的核心焦点，尤其是Siri的表现问题。
• 数据隐私和伦理问题在讨论中占据重要位置，Perfmode和Frankfrank13对此有不同解读。
• 与竞争对手的比较（如Google、OpenAI）也是讨论的重要方面，部分评论认为Apple在这些方面表现不足。
• 对Apple未来在AI领域潜力的看法存在分歧，部分评论持乐观态度，而另一些则表示怀疑。

We introduce two multilingual, multimodal foundation language models that power Apple Intelligence features across Apple devices and services: (i) a â¼3B-parameter on-device model optimized for Apple silicon through architectural innovations such as KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantization-aware training; and (ii) a scalable server model built on a novel Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts (PT-MoE) transformer that combines track parallelism, mixture-of-experts sparse computation, and interleaved globalâlocal attention to deliver high quality with competitive cost on Appleâs Private Cloud Compute platform. Both models are trained on large-scale multilingual and multimodal datasets sourced via responsible web crawling, licensed corpora, and high-quality synthetic data, then further refined with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on a new asynchronous platform. The resulting models support several additional languages while understanding images and executing tool calls. In public benchmarks and human evaluations, both the server model and the on-device model match or surpass comparably sized open baselines.
A new Swift-centric Foundation Models framework exposes guided generation, constrained tool calling, and LoRA adapter fine-tuning, allowing developers to integrate these capabilities with a few lines of code. The latest advancements in Apple Intelligence models are grounded in our Responsible AI approach with safeguards like content filtering and locale-specific evaluation, as well as our commitment to protecting our usersâ privacy with innovations like Private Cloud Compute.
This paper provides technical details for Updates to Apple's On-Device and Server Foundation Language Models, introduced on June 9, 2025, in this
post

Apple Intelligence is comprised of multiple highly-capable generative models that are specialized for our usersâ everyday tasks, and can adapt on the fly for their current activity. The foundation models built into Apple Intelligence have been fine-tuned for user experiences such as writing and refining text, prioritizing and summarizing notifications, creating playful images for conversations with family and friends, and taking in-app actions to simplify interactions across apps.

data.title: Perfume reviews
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文简要讨论了尝试各种“前卫”香水及其他香水的体验，分享了作者的喜好和不喜欢的香水，并最终透露购买了两款香水：Acqua di Sale和Kyoto Incense。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：香水爱好、购买建议、香水行业及其争议

不同观点：
• **香水作为一种艺术形式**：Clamchop认为香水是一种被误解的艺术形式，与音乐和绘画类似，值得更多欣赏。他认为许多人因为对香水的不了解而对其抱有偏见。

• **香水购买和收藏的经验**：
   - ericmay分享了对Relique d’Amour香水的积极体验，并提到在巴黎的香水店有丰富的试香经历。
   - Scene_Cast2建议通过购买小样或分装来探索香水，并提到一些专门提供分装的卖家，如Surrender to Chance和LuckyScent。
   - ggm则抱怨香水品牌常常停产自己喜爱的香味，指出香水市场的不可预测性。

• **对特定品牌和香水的推荐**：
   - harimau777推荐Black Phoenix Alchemy Lab的香水。
   - spapas82认为大多数香水缺乏独特性，尤其对男性香水市场感到失望。
   - bravura提到虽然自己讨厌香水，但对Christopher Brosius的创作非常着迷，尤其是其独特的香味如"In the library"和"Wild hunt"。

• **对香水行业的批评和健康考虑**：
   - v5v3指出高档香水使用更纯净的成分，但主流香水可能含有廉价的化学物质，对健康不利。
   - aussieguy1234建议为了省钱可以选择从好的克隆香水商那里购买，而不是追求品牌香水。

补充讨论：
• **香水描述和评价的困难**：
   - Clamchop提到香水描述往往使用非常抽象和华丽的语言，因为普通人的气味词汇有限。
   - mk_stjames调侃某些网站的评论质量，暗示对香水的讨论常常过于夸张。

• **地域和文化差异**：
   - AYBABTME提到在首尔的Sinsa社区有一条专门的香水街，那里有很多实验性的香水工作。

• **香水保存和体验的技巧**：
   - DobarDabar建议通过闻咖啡豆来解决嗅觉疲劳问题，这是许多香水店常用的方法。

争议的焦点：
• **香水市场的不可预测性和品牌忠诚度**：ggm抱怨自己喜欢的香水被品牌停产，这引发了对消费者选择权和品牌策略的讨论。

• **香水的价值和购买建议**：一些人如spapas82对大多数香水的独特性表示怀疑，而aussieguy1234则提出通过购买克隆香水来节省开支，这涉及到品牌价值和消费者选择的争议。

data.title: All AI models might be the same
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI模型是否能通过学习通用语言来理解鲸鱼交流或破解古代文字。作者通过一个名为“墨索里尼还是面包”的游戏说明人类具有共通的语义感知，这种感知源于我们对世界的共同理解。文章进一步解释，AI模型的智能体现于其对数据的压缩能力，压缩能力越强，模型对世界的理解就越深。这种压缩与智能之间的双重关系表明，更大的语言模型能够更好地压缩数据并实现泛化。最终，模型在无法进一步压缩数据时才会开始真正泛化，这揭示了模型从记忆到泛化的转变过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）是否会趋同以及其表征和理解现实的能力

不同观点：
• [seeknotfind] 反对柏拉图式的普遍性观点，认为即使某些事物对很多人来说相似，它们本质上并不相同。例如，绿色对他来说是祖母夏天草坪的气味，这种主观体验无法被简化为统一的现实模型。
• [lsy] 质疑“共享现实统计模型”的概念，指出诸如“肯塔基德比”等例子是历史和文化的产物，而非现实的核心部分。模型趋同可能只是因为训练数据集的同质性，而非反映了某种客观现实。
• [coffeecoders] 对通过AI解码鲸歌或古语言持怀疑态度，认为语言的理解依赖于共享的背景经验，而AI缺乏这种与人类相似的经验基础。
• [IAmNotACellist] 认为LLM确实基于人类集体作品趋同于某种现实表征，但要提升AI的理解能力，需要提供实时感官输入、模拟荷尔蒙变化等更复杂的机制。
• [TheSaifurRahman] 强调不同知识水平之间的匹配问题，指出在专家和普通人间可能存在语义距离的差异，这同样适用于对古代文本的理解。
• [streptomycin] 质疑某些推理游戏的逻辑，认为许多事物可能会有相同的答案，但这并不意味着它们本质上相似。
• [megaloblasto] 认为如果所有模型趋同于相同的智能，那么开源模型可能会使专有模型变得过时，这对开放源码是有利的。
• [kindkang2024] 使用道家思想来解释，认为语言模型可能会趋同于某种“道”，即所有语言和文化背后的共同意志。
• [stillpointlab] 直觉上认为不同LLM可能揭示了一种单一的智能，但同时也警惕确认偏误的影响。并提到海德格尔的语言偏好，认为某些语言中的双关语可能隐藏着深层次的哲学真理。
• [somethingsome] 对“事物关系唯一性”的观点持怀疑态度，认为即使在相同词汇下，不同意义排列可能会导致不同的压缩方案，而非趋同于一种最佳方案。
